title: Soft Gluten-Free Pretzels, Coated or Flavored

content.title: About
content.content: Soft gluten‑free pretzels are baked from gluten‑free grains such as rice, corn or buckwheat, combined with starch and a small amount of yeast. They can be coated with salt, cheese, spices or sweet glazes. The pretzels have a tender crumb, a light aroma and are suitable for people with gluten intolerance.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gluten‑free pretzels are a popular snack for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.
Traditional German pretzels are knotted and crunchy, while the soft versions are usually flat and pliable.
Coatings may include sea salt, cheese powder, spicy blends, cinnamon‑sugar, or chocolate glaze.
Using gluten‑free flours allows the pretzel to keep a crisp exterior with a soft interior.
The U.S. gluten‑free snack market is growing at over 12 % annually.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Most varieties contain little to no added sugar, making them suitable for moderate consumption.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice and corn flours supply niacin, thiamine and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Completely safe for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Grain allergies
items.content: Some gluten‑free blends may contain soy protein or dairy, which can trigger allergies.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Salted versions can be high in sodium; choose unsalted or lightly salted if you have hypertension.

items.title: Additive content
items.content: Glazes and flavorings may include artificial sweeteners or preservatives.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Despite being gluten‑free, pretzels are still calorie‑dense due to starch and coating fats.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy pretzels as a snack on their own, pair with dips (hummus, yogurt sauce), add to salads, or use in appetizer platters. Sweet‑coated pretzels pair well with coffee or tea.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life keep them in the refrigerator to maintain crispness. Avoid moisture, which can make pretzels soggy.
